non_blocking_notes: Both prior-gate repairs were independently verified rather than taken on trust. Repair 1: I reconstructed the pre-repair expression in a scratch script (uv run python /tmp/chk_old.py) and observed the old defect exactly — dtype Datetime(time_unit='us', time_zone='America/Chicago') carrying wall clock 05:00 — so the new assertions `converted.data.schema['time'] == pl.Datetime('us')` and `== [datetime(2026, 1, 15, 11, 0)]` both fail against the old code and are a genuine regression guard, not a restatement.

Repair 2 was verified as a real chokepoint, not an assumed one: uv run python /tmp/chk_patch2.py monkeypatched pl.read_parquet and called load_packaged_catalogue_artifact on the real packaged usgs_nwis catalogue directory; it printed 'intercepted: to_utc consulted the catalogue'. src/rivretrieve/_internal/catalogues/artifact.py:125 and native.py:50 both resolve pl.read_parquet as a module attribute at call time, so the patch cannot be bypassed by an import-style rebinding the way the earlier vacuous patch was.

The plan authored four tests in tests/test_utc.py; the head contains five (the repair added test_to_utc_tz_aware_time_dtype_becomes_naive), so the plan's `1622 + 4 = 1626` arithmetic is stale by one. The extra test lives inside the plan's own write-set file and exists solely to guard the repaired defect. The PR body claims '1627 passed, 2 skipped'; my own `uv run pytest -q` reported exactly `1627 passed, 2 skipped in 352.40s`, so the body states the true observed number and does not repeat the plan's stale count. It could have said in one line that the repair added a fifth test, but nothing in the body is inaccurate.

Duplicated logic worth a follow-up, not a block: `_tzinfo` in src/rivretrieve/_internal/utc.py re-splits and re-parses the ±HH:MM offset that ZoneValue.__post_init__ (src/rivretrieve/_internal/engine.py:367-373) has already validated and parsed with the identical `(int(part) for part in value[1:].split(':'))` idiom. A `ZoneValue.tzinfo`/`utcoffset` accessor on the domain type would leave one parser instead of two that must stay in sync.

`naive_dtype = pl.Datetime(time_dtype.time_unit) if isinstance(time_dtype, pl.Datetime) else time_dtype` carries an unreachable else branch under the enforced ObservationDataSchema, and the same isinstance test is then repeated on the next line. Harmless defensiveness, but two guards for one condition reads heavier than the surrounding code.

Conversion round-trips through Python `datetime`, which is microsecond-resolution, so a hypothetical Datetime('ns') input would silently lose sub-microsecond precision. I confirmed the time unit itself is preserved and values are correct at us/ms/ns (uv run python /tmp/chk_utc.py printed `ns: Datetime(time_unit='ns', time_zone=None) [2025-12-31 18:45]`). The canonical baseline is datetime[us], and the plan mandates per-row Python conversion, so this is inherent to the contract rather than a defect in it.

The plan states an empty valid result must return a new schema-identical empty result, but no test covers it. I exercised it manually: `empty ok (0, 5) True` — shape preserved and `data.schema == ObservationDataSchema.polars_schema`. An empty-frame case would be a cheap addition to a later step.

Refusal-path robustness beyond the contract: a null in `time_zone` would pass the `.eq('unknown').sum()` preflight and then reach `ZoneValue(None)`, raising TypeError rather than FatalContractError. The five-column schema plus the ZoneValue domain make this unreachable for a valid ObservationResult, so it is out of scope for this step.

The worktree carries an untracked `pytest-of-nicolaslazaro/` directory (a pytest tmp-dir artifact present before this review began). It is untracked, absent from the commit, and does not affect the artifact under review, but it is not covered by .gitignore and will keep showing up in `git status`.
summary:
This change should land. It is exactly one commit (ff559ed) above the base, with no tag, no attribution trailer, no version movement (__version__ stays 0.1.49, pyproject.toml and uv.lock untouched), and pr-body.md left untracked. The diff touches precisely the five write-set files and nothing else; the only edit to a pre-existing test adds `to_utc` to the exact public-name set and adds `assert rivretrieve.to_utc is to_utc` — no assertion is weakened or deleted, and no suppression is introduced.

The decided zone semantics are implemented as specified. Each row is converted by its own published zone via `_convert_wall_clock`, dispatched through the existing ZoneValue domain; no offset is promoted to an IANA identifier (`_tzinfo` builds a fixed `timezone` for ±HH:MM and only calls ZoneInfo for a slash-bearing identifier); nothing in the module reads a catalogue, tz_cd, station metadata, or provider config, and the module performs no I/O at all. The multi-offset USGS span (-06:00 then -05:00 in one station/product) converts row by row to 07:30/08:30 rather than being rejected. `unknown` is the sole rejection condition, counted over the whole frame before any conversion, so the refusal is genuinely atomic — the monkeypatched `_convert_wall_clock` probe is resolved as a module global inside the comprehension, so that patch really does intercept, and the test observes `calls == []` with the source frame unchanged. The message matches the fixed template character for character, naming the provider from provenance and the affected-row count of 2 (not a distinct-station or distinct-zone count). The required denotation docstring is present verbatim.

Both repairs are correct and complete, and I confirmed each rather than inheriting the prior gate's conclusion. Repair 1 now derives a naive dtype from the input time unit and strips tzinfo before reading the wall clock; reproducing the old expression showed exactly the reported defect (05:00 stamped America/Chicago), which the new test's dtype and value assertions both catch. Repair 2's added patches on pl.read_parquet/pl.scan_parquet are the real chokepoint every packaged read funnels through, proven empirically against the actual usgs_nwis artifact directory. The repair introduces no new defect: I checked empty frames, ms/us/ns time units, and an already-+00:00 row, all correct.

Gates are green at this head: `uv run ruff format --check` (164 files already formatted), `uv run ruff check` (All checks passed), `uv run ty check src` (All checks passed), and `uv run pytest -q` reporting 1627 passed, 2 skipped — the 1622 baseline plus the five tests in tests/test_utc.py, matching the PR body's claim. The worktree is tracked-clean. Remaining observations are maintainability preferences (a duplicated offset parser that ZoneValue could own, one unreachable dtype branch) and an uncovered empty-frame case I verified by hand; none of them should hold up this merge.
